note.text: Every recommendation engine on the planet got rewarded for finding the edge of disagreement, because conflict is sticky and sticky is profitable. Flip the optimization target and the model behaves completely differently: instead of ranking by outrage, it ranks by overlap, surfacing the boring, unglamorous patch of agreement buried under the loudest ten percent of any debate. That patch exists in almost every dataset of human opinion, polling and employee surveys included, which means most organizations aren't lacking consensus, they're lacking a scoring function that rewards finding it. The algorithm was never the villain; the loss function was.
